review_scope: Read-only source/workflow review and inspection of saved serial result/NetCDF files; no compile, fixture, model, or solver was launched by reviewer.

independent_array_checks.method: Read existing O0/O2 NetCDF outputs with Python netCDF4; no test/compile was run.

source_review.integer_and_float_transfer: Fixture tests 3x5 unique INTEGER32 values, WRF_DOUBLE converted to REAL4, and direct REAL32 input to REAL4 output, including exact backend readback and low-level NetCDF type/rank/extent inquiries.
source_review.memory_order: Uppercase ZZ and lowercase zz are exercised; qq/QQ rejection and absence of an unsupported variable are checked.
source_review.failure_receipts: Runner persists PREPARED/STARTED/terminal child journals atomically with fsync, writes actual child RC before output interpretation, bounds waits, and attempts process-group termination/reap on exceptions. This review inspected the code but did not inject a failure into the new runner. The saved serial run has eight clean terminal RC=0 children.
source_review.ci: The standalone-columns job is triggered by WRF/test/rrtmgp/** and workflow changes; it installs required compiler/NetCDF tools, runs the test, and uploads receipt/log/json/stdout/stderr/f90 artifacts with if: always().
source_review.scope: The fixture invokes ext_ncd backend APIs and a synthetic optional MPI broadcast wrapper. It does not run WRF module_io, a full WRF build/forecast, or RRTMGP; documentation and receipt state this limit.

nonblocking_documentation_note: Clarify that the supplied axis order is preserved in the Fortran NetCDF API view. The actual files inspected through the C/Python NetCDF view expose dimensions as (Time, independent_n, vertical_k), the conventional reversal of Fortran dimension order. The Fortran low-level inquiry in the fixture checks (vertical_k, independent_n, Time). This is consistent with the observed interface behavior, but the current phrase that order survives 'NetCDF definition' could be read as a C-visible on-disk order claim.
verdict_limit: The fixture validates the focused backend storage/readback contract only; it is not a full WRF checkpoint/restart integration test and does not establish radiation or active stochastic-forcing correctness.
